dek: Five Mount Rainier waterfalls with walk lengths, fees and snow timing. Narada Falls is a 0.2-mile walk and Comet Falls is 1.8 miles one way.
overview: Mount Rainier rises 14,410 feet and is the most glaciated peak in the contiguous United States, with five major rivers flowing off the ice. The park names Narada Falls as one of dozens of waterfalls fed by glacier and snowmelt creeks.

We cover five waterfalls, all filed under Eatonville: Narada, Silver, Comet, Christine and Carter Falls. Narada, Silver and Comet have published walk lengths, all one way. Christine Falls is described as a waterfall framed by a stone bridge, and neither Christine nor Carter Falls has a distance in our files.
fallsIntro: Narada Falls has an upper viewpoint and a lower trail. The lower trail drops about 200 feet and climbs back up.
plan: Narada Falls is the quick stop at 0.2 mile one way (0.4 mile round trip). The park's notes call the upper viewpoint easy and the lower trail moderate and slippery, and say the lower trail is best when it is snow-free in summer and early fall. The upper pullout is open year-round.
Silver Falls is 0.3 mile one way. Comet Falls is the longer hike at 1.8 miles one way on the Van Trump Trail.
flow: The nearest gauge with a complete record is the Cowlitz River at Packwood (USGS 14226500), about 11 miles from Silver Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in May at about 2,716 cubic feet per second and was lowest in September at about 444.

Rainier's waterfalls are fed by glaciers and snowmelt, so they rise with melt and with rain. The park's weather page says snow stays between 5,000 and 8,000 feet well into mid-July, so a May or June peak downstream doesn't mean the trails near the falls are snow-free.
feesLead: The vehicle pass is $30 for seven days, and the park said in February 2026 that it will not use timed entry this year.
access: Instead of timed entry, the park says it will manage parking when lots fill, so arrive early. The weather page says late July and August are generally the driest, warmest months, though rain is still possible.
safety: Narada Falls' lower trail is the one with a posted hazard: about 200 feet of descent, slippery, and a poor idea when it is snow-covered. The upper pullout is the year-round alternative. We have no matching warnings on file for Comet Falls or Silver Falls.
